title: Complaint process was fair
article: Writing for the three-judge panel, Chief Judge Lance Finch dismissed Julie Berg's appeal of the police complaint hearing decision that her brother's death at the hands of the VPD was justified.
B.C.'s highest court may have finally doused the long-running, corrosive dispute between the Vancouver police department and the sister of dead home invader Jeffrey Michael Berg.
Writing for the three-judge panel, Chief Judge Lance Finch dismissed Julie Berg's appeal of the police complaint hearing decision that her brother's death at the hands of the VPD was justified.
Berg, who has waged a five-year fight to learn the truth about the tragedy, claimed she was denied the right to fully participate in the hearing, that it was unfair and its conclusions wrong.

But Finch tossed her arguments and said there was no reason for the court to interfere with the police complaint ruling. He said her right to participate in the hearing was circumscribed by law and there was nothing wrong with that.

The province's high bench said complainants' participation was expressly limited "to the making of oral or written submissions after all the evidence is called" and they had "no right to lead evidence or cross-examine witnesses."
Berg's secondary plea that she lacked funding to adequately participate in the hearing and required state support also fell on deaf ears.
She might not like it, the court said, still she was treated fairly.
